rights_note: A US federal census schedule of 1910, in the public domain. Read for who lived at an address; no asset is derived from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-05 (T-3382) from the Internet Archive's page images by eye; the schedules are handwritten and the item has no usable OCR. Only the Prairie Avenue households of the 1904 People cards were read closely; the rest of each sheet was not transcribed.
note: The census of 15 April 1910 lists every person whose usual place of abode was the dwelling, by relationship to the head, with age, and for each married or widowed woman the number of children she had borne and the number living. It is six years after the 1904 scene: it is read here for the CHILDREN of the 1904 households, both those who were already at home in 1904 (then younger) and those born after it, and for the relationships the Blue Book does not print.
what_it_supplies: the children at home in April 1910, by name, with age and relationship to the head
the mothers' counts of children born and living
relationships the Blue Book never prints (a son, a daughter, a sister, a niece)
what_it_does_not_supply: anything on 1 July 1904; a child seen in 1910 is placed in the 1904 house only by inference from age and the family's listing
children already grown and gone by 1910
households not on Prairie Avenue (the Lowdens, gone by 1910)
